stem: Why does Perthes disease have a poorer prognosis when it presents in a child older than 8 years?

options.text: The growth plates have already closed

explanation: Poor healing potential is the reason older children with Perthes disease tend to have a worse prognosis. Their ability to remodel bone and revascularise the femoral head is reduced compared with younger children.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because older children have less biological capacity for the bone remodelling and revascularisation needed for recovery.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because Perthes disease is confined to the femoral head and does not spread to the spine.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because surgery may still be possible; the prognosis is limited by the underlying healing potential rather than technical impossibility.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the growth plates are not the main issue here; the problem is reduced biological recovery with increasing age.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the femoral head can revascularise, but this process is less effective in older children.

source.hint: Focus on the biological limitations regarding bone regeneration that occur as a child grows older.
